html:
The Ngarkat are a recorded Aboriginal group of South Australia, of the mallee and sandy heath of the Ninety Mile Desert, south of the Murray River near the Victorian border. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their lands linked the mallee peoples of Victoria with the river peoples of the lower Murray, such as the Ngarrindjeri. Water was scarce, and people relied on soaks and on water stored in mallee roots. Little of their language was recorded, and it has been loosely grouped with that of the Peramangk, though not by linguists. Ngarkat Conservation Park now keeps their name. Another neighbour on the map is the Bindjali. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
